summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to coat LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 (LNMO) cathode materials with an amorphous FePO4 layer. The FePO4 coating acts as a lithium-ion reservoir, enhancing high-voltage stability by preventing electrolyte oxidation and Mn dissolution. The ALD process uses ferrocene, ozone, trimethyl phosphate, and water as precursors at 300 °C. The coating improves cycling stability and capacity retention, with the best performance observed at 10 ALD cycles.
evidence: Amorphous FePO4 has been widely studied as cathode materials for both lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). In our recent work, we successfully synthesized FePO4 via ALD process, which has also been demonstrated by Fjellvåg and coworkers to deliver a discharge capacity of above 140 mAh g–1. The preparation process of LNMO powders is described in the experimental section. Amorphous FePO4 was deposited at 300 °C by using ferrocene (FeCp2), ozone (O3), trimethyl phosphate (TMPO), and distilled water (H2O) as precursors in a Savannah 100 ALD system.
